entries.definition_ko: 「요새」라는 뜻이니, 아모스가(아모스 9:7) 아람 사람이 한때 「올라온」 땅이라 말한 곳이다. 곧 그들이 팔레스타인 북쪽 지역으로 옮겨 오기 전에 살던 땅인 듯하다. (길의 자리에 대하여는 견해가 갈리니, 어떤 이는 남쪽 마르두스 강가에 있는 메대의 성 카르마와 같은 곳으로 보고, 어떤 이는 아르메니아의 쿠르 강가에 둔다.—편집자)

entries.definition: (fortress of Moab), one of the two chief strongholds of Moab, the other being Ar of Moab. The name occurs only in (Isaiah 15:1) though the place is probably referred to under the names of Kir-heres, Kir-harseth, etc. It is almost identical with the name Kerak, by which the site of an important city in a high and very strong position at the southeast of the Dead Sea is known at this day. Its situation is truly remarkable. It is built upon the top of a steep hill, surrounded by a deep and narrow valley, which again is completely enclosed by mountains rising higher than the town and overlooking it on all sides.
entries.definition_ko: 「모압의 요새」라는 뜻이니, 모압의 두 큰 산성 가운데 하나요 다른 하나는 모압 아르이다. 이 이름은 오직 이사야 15:1에만 나오나, 이곳은 아마 길하레스나 길하레셋 같은 이름으로 언급될 것이다. 이 이름은 오늘날 사해 남동쪽 높고 매우 험한 자리에 있는 중요한 성의 터를 가리키는 케락이라는 이름과 거의 같다. 그 자리는 참으로 남다르다. 가파른 언덕 꼭대기에 세워졌고 깊고 좁은 골짜기가 둘렀으며, 그 골짜기를 다시 그 성읍보다 높이 솟아 사방에서 내려다보는 산들이 온전히 에워쌌다.

entries.definition: (brick fortress), (2 Kings 3:25) Kir-ha’resh, (Isaiah 16:11) Kir-har’es, (Jeremiah 48:31,36) These four names are all applied to one place, probably Kir Of MoabOF MOAB, which see.
entries.definition_ko: 「벽돌 요새」라는 뜻이니 열왕기하 3:25에 나오고, 이사야 16:11에는 길하레스, 예레미야 48:31,36에는 길헤레스라 나온다. 이 네 이름은 모두 한곳을 가리키니 아마 모압 길일 것이다. 모압 길 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: apparently an ancient or archaic word, meaning a city or town. It may be compared to the word “burg” or “bury” in our own language. Closely related to Kiriah is Kereth, apparently a Phoenician form, which occurs occasionally. (Job 29:7; Proverbs 8:3) As a proper name it appears in the Bible under the forms of Kerioth, Kartah, Kartan, besides those immediately following.
entries.definition_ko: 오래된 옛 말인 듯하며 성이나 성읍을 뜻한다. 우리 말의 「고을」이나 「마을」에 견줄 수 있다. 기랴와 가까운 말이 케렛이니 베니게 말꼴인 듯하며 이따금 나온다(욥기 29:7; 잠언 8:3). 고유한 이름으로는 성경에 그리욧, 가르다, 가르단이라는 꼴로, 또 바로 뒤에 오는 이름들로 나온다.

entries.definition: [KIRJATHAIM]
entries.definition_ko: 기랴다임 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: (two cities), a place in Moab the palaces of which were threatened by Amos with destruction by fire, (Amos 2:2) unless indeed the word means simply “the cities,” which is probably the case also in (Jeremiah 48:4)
entries.definition_ko: 「두 성읍」이라는 뜻이니, 모압의 한 곳이요 아모스가 그 궁궐을 불로 사르겠다고 위협한 곳이다(아모스 2:2). 다만 이 말이 그저 「그 성읍들」을 뜻할 수도 있으니, 예레미야 48:4도 아마 그러할 것이다.

entries.definition: (a city), the last of the cities enumerated as belonging to the tribe of Benjamin, (Joshua 18:28) probably identical with the better-known place Kirjath-jearim.
entries.definition_ko: 「성읍」이라는 뜻이니, 베냐민 지파에 속한 것으로 헤아려진 성읍 가운데 마지막이며(여호수아 18:28) 아마 더 널리 알려진 기럇여아림과 같은 곳일 것이다.

entries.definition: (the city of Arba), an early name of the city which after the conquest is generally known as Hebron. (Joshua 14:15; Judges 1:10) The identity of Kirjath-arba with Hebron is constantly asserted. (Genesis 23:2; 35:27; Joshua 14:15; 15:13,54; 20:7; 21:11)
entries.definition_ko: 「아르바의 성읍」이라는 뜻이니, 정복 뒤에 흔히 헤브론이라 알려진 성의 이른 이름이다(여호수아 14:15; 사사기 1:10). 기럇아르바가 헤브론과 같은 곳이라는 것이 늘 말해진다(창세기 23:2; 창세기 35:27; 여호수아 14:15; 여호수아 15:13,54; 여호수아 20:7; 여호수아 21:11).

entries.definition: (city of forests), an abbreviated form of the name Kirjath-jearim, which occurs only in (Ezra 2:25)
entries.definition_ko: 「숲의 성읍」이라는 뜻이니, 기럇여아림이라는 이름을 줄인 꼴이요 오직 에스라 2:25에만 나온다.

entries.definition: [KIRJATH-JEARIM]
entries.definition_ko: 기럇여아림 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: (city of streets), a place to which Balak accompanied Balaam immediately after his arrival in Moab, (Numbers 22:39) and which is nowhere else mentioned. It appears to have lain between the Arnon (Wady Mojeb) and Bamoth-baal. Comp. vs. (Numbers 22:36) and Numb 22:41
entries.definition_ko: 「거리의 성읍」이라는 뜻이니, 발락이 모압에 이른 발람과 함께 곧바로 간 곳이요(민수기 22:39) 다른 데에는 나오지 않는다. 아르논(와디 모젭)과 바못바알 사이에 있었던 듯하다. 민수기 22:36과 민수기 22:41을 견주라.

entries.definition: (the city of forests), first mentioned as one of the four cities of the Gibeonites, (Joshua 9:17) it next occurs as one of the landmarks of the northern boundary of Judah, ch (Joshua 15:9) and as the point at which the western and southern boundaries of Benjamin coincided, ch. (Joshua 18:14,15) and in the last two passages we find that it bore another, perhaps earlier, name—that of the great Canaanite deity Baal, namely Baalahand KIRJATH-BAAL. At this place the ark remained for twenty years. (1 Samuel 7:2) At the close of that time Kirjath-jearim lost its sacred treasure, on its removal by David to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. (1 Chronicles 13:5,6; 2 Chronicles 1:4; 2 Samuel 6:2) etc. To Eusebius and Jerome it appears to have been well known. They describe it as a village at the ninth mile between Jerusalem and Diospolis (Lydda). These requirements are exactly fulfilled in the small modern village of Kuriet-elEnab—now usually known as Abu Gosh, from the robber chief whose headquarters it was—on the road from Jaffa and Jerusalem.
entries.definition_ko: 「숲의 성읍」이라는 뜻이니, 기브온 사람의 네 성읍 가운데 하나로 처음 언급되고(여호수아 9:17), 다음으로는 유다의 북쪽 경계를 나타내는 곳 가운데 하나로(여호수아 15:9), 또 베냐민의 서쪽과 남쪽 경계가 만나는 지점으로 나온다(여호수아 18:14,15). 뒤의 두 곳에서 우리는 이 성읍이 또 다른, 아마 더 이른 이름을 지녔음을 보니, 곧 큰 가나안 신 바알의 이름을 딴 바알라와 기럇바알이다. 이곳에 궤가 스무 해를 머물렀다(사무엘상 7:2). 그 기간이 끝날 때에 다윗이 궤를 가드 사람 오벧에돔의 집으로 옮기매 기럇여아림은 그 거룩한 보배를 잃었다(역대상 13:5,6; 역대하 1:4; 사무엘하 6:2 등). 유세비우스와 제롬에게는 이곳이 잘 알려져 있었던 듯하다. 그들은 이곳을 예루살렘과 디오스폴리스(룻다) 사이 아홉째 마일에 있는 마을이라 적는다. 이 조건은 욥바와 예루살렘 사이 길가에 있는 작은 마을 쿠리에트 엘에납에 꼭 들어맞으니, 이곳은 이제 흔히 아부 고쉬라 부르는데 그곳을 근거지로 삼았던 도적 두목의 이름에서 왔다.

entries.definition: (city of books). [Debir]
entries.definition_ko: 「책의 성읍」이라는 뜻이다. 드빌 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: (city of books). (Joshua 15:15,16; Judges 1:11,12) [Debir]
entries.definition_ko: 「책의 성읍」이라는 뜻이다(여호수아 15:15,16; 사사기 1:11,12). 드빌 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: (a bow). • The father of Saul; a Benjamite of the family of Matri. (B.C. 1095.) • Son of Jehiel and uncle to the preceding. (1 Chronicles 9:36) • A Benjamite, great-grandfather of Mordecai. (Esther 2:5) • A Merarite of the house of Mahli, of the tribe of Levi. (1 Chronicles 23:21,22; 24:28,29)
entries.definition_ko: 「활」이라는 뜻. (1) 사울의 아버지이니 마드리 집안에 속한 베냐민 사람이다. (주전 1095년.) (2) 여이엘의 아들이요 앞의 사람의 삼촌이다(역대상 9:36). (3) 베냐민 사람이요 모르드개의 증조부이다(에스더 2:5). (4) 레위 지파 말리 집안에 속한 므라리 사람이다(역대상 23:21,22; 역대상 24:28,29).

entries.definition: (bow of Jehovah), a Merarite, and father of ancestor of Ethan the minstrel. (1 Chronicles 6:44)
entries.definition_ko: 「여호와의 활」이라는 뜻이니, 므라리 사람이요 노래하는 이 에단의 아버지 곧 조상이다(역대상 6:44).

entries.definition: (hardness), one of the towns on the boundary of the tribe of Issachar, (Joshua 19:20) which with its suburbs was allotted to the Gershonite Levites. (Joshua 21:28) Authorized Version Kishon.
entries.definition_ko: 「굳음」이라는 뜻이니, 잇사갈 지파의 경계에 있던 성읍 가운데 하나요(여호수아 19:20) 그 들과 함께 게르손 자손 레위 사람에게 나누어 주었다(여호수아 21:28). 흠정역은 기손이라 한다.

entries.definition: (winding), The river, a torrent or winter stream of central Palestine, the scene of two of the grandest achievements of Israelitish history—the defeat of Sisera, Judges 4, and the destruction of the prophets of Baal by Elijah. (1 Kings 18:40) The Nahr Mukutta, the modern representative of the Kishon, is the drain by which the waters of the plain of Esdraelon and of the mountains which enclose that plain find their way through the plain of Acre to the Mediterranean. The part of the Kishon at which the prophets of Baal were slaughtered by Elijah was doubtless close below the spot on Carmel where the sacrifice had taken place.
entries.definition_ko: 「굽이치는」이라는 뜻이니, 기손 강은 팔레스타인 가운데 지역의 급류 곧 겨울에 흐르는 시내요, 이스라엘 역사에서 가장 웅장한 두 일이 있었던 무대이다. 곧 시스라를 무찌른 일(사사기 4장)과 엘리야가 바알의 선지자들을 없앤 일이다(열왕기상 18:40). 오늘 기손을 가리키는 나르 무쿠타는 이스르엘 평지와 그 평지를 두른 산들의 물이 악고 평지를 거쳐 지중해로 흘러가는 물길이다. 엘리야가 바알의 선지자들을 죽인 기손의 그 자리는 틀림없이 제사를 드린 갈멜의 그곳 바로 아래였을 것이다.

entries.definition: (winding), an inaccurate mode of representing the name Kishon. (Psalms 83:9)
entries.definition_ko: 「굽이치는」이라는 뜻이니, 기손이라는 이름을 정확하지 않게 적은 꼴이다(시편 83:9).

entries.definition: Kissing the lips by way of affectionate salutation was customary among near relatives of both sexes, in both patriarchal and later times. (Genesis 29:11; Song of Solomon 8:1) Between individuals of the same sex, and in a limited degree between those of different sexes, the kiss on the cheek as a mark of respect or an act of salutation has at all times been customary in the East, and can hardly be said to be extinct even in Europe. In the Christian Church the kiss of charity was practiced not only as a friendly salutation, but as an act symbolical of love and Christian brotherhood. (Romans 16:16; 1 Corinthians 16:20; 2 Corinthians 13:12; 1 Thessalonians 5:6; 1 Peter 5:14) It was embodied in the earlier Christian offices, and has been continued in some of those now in use. Among the Arabs the women and children kiss the beards of their husbands or fathers. The superior returns the salute by a kiss on the forehead. In Egypt an inferior kisses the hand of a superior, generally on the back, but sometimes, as a special favor, on the palm also. To testify abject submission, and in asking favors, the feet are often kissed instead of the hand. The written decrees of a sovereign are kissed in token of respect; even the ground is sometimes kissed by Orientals int he fullness of their submission. (Genesis 41:40; 1 Samuel 24:8; Psalms 72:9) etc. Kissing is spoken of in Scripture as a mark of respect or adoration to idols. (1 Kings 19:18; Hosea 13:2)
entries.definition_ko:
다정한 인사로 입을 맞추는 일은 족장 때에도 그 뒤에도 남녀를 가리지 않고 가까운 친척 사이에서 늘 있는 일이었다(창세기 29:11; 아가 8:1). 같은 성 사이에서, 또 얼마쯤은 다른 성 사이에서도 존경의 표나 인사로 뺨에 입 맞추는 일이 동방에서는 늘 있었고, 유럽에서도 아주 사라졌다고 하기 어렵다. 그리스도의 교회에서 사랑의 입맞춤은 다만 다정한 인사로만이 아니라 사랑과 그리스도 안의 형제 됨을 나타내는 행위로 행해졌다(로마서 16:16; 고린도전서 16:20; 고린도후서 13:12; 데살로니가전서 5:26; 베드로전서 5:14). 이는 더 이른 그리스도교 예식에 담겼고 오늘 쓰이는 얼마의 예식에도 이어져 있다. 아라비아 사람 가운데서 여인과 아이들은 남편이나 아버지의 수염에 입을 맞춘다. 윗사람은 이마에 입 맞춤으로 그 인사에 답한다. 애굽에서는 아랫사람이 윗사람의 손등에 입을 맞추고, 때로는 남다른 은혜로 손바닥에도 입을 맞춘다. 지극한 복종을 나타내거나 은혜를 구할 때에는 손 대신 발에 입을 맞추는 일이 흔하다. 임금이 글로 내린 명령은 존경의 표로 입을 맞춘다. 동방 사람은 복종이 가득할 때에 땅에 입을 맞추기도 한다(창세기 41:40; 사무엘상 24:8; 시편 72:9 등). 성경은 입맞춤을 우상에게 바치는 존경 또는 경배의 표로도 말한다(열왕기상 19:18; 호세아 13:2).
※ 원문 오류: 1 Thessalonians 5:6 → 데살로니가전서 5:26
※ 판정 근거: 본문 대조. 「거룩하게 입맞춤으로 모든 형제에게 문안하라」는 데살로니가전서 5:26이요, 5:6은 자지 말고 깨어 정신을 차리라는 절이다.

entries.definition: (Heb. ayyah), a rapacious and keen-sighted bird of prey belonging to the hawk family. The Hebrew word thus rendered occurs in three passages— (Leviticus 11:14; 14:13; Job 28:7) In the two former it is translated “kite” in the Authorized Version, in the latter “vulture.” It is enumerated among the twenty names of birds mentioned in (14:1) ... which were considered unclean by the Mosaic law and forbidden to be used as food by the Israelites.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리 말로 아야이니, 매 무리에 드는 사납고 눈 밝은 새이다. 이렇게 옮긴 히브리 낱말은 세 곳에 나온다(레위기 11:14; 신명기 14:13; 욥기 28:7). 앞의 두 곳에서 흠정역은 「솔개」로, 뒤엣곳에서는 「독수리」로 옮겼다. 이 새는 신명기 14:1 이하에 나오는 스무 가지 새 이름 가운데 하나로 헤아려지니, 이것들은 모세의 율법이 부정하다 하여 이스라엘 사람이 먹지 못하게 한 것들이다.

entries.definition: (man’s wall), one of the towns of Judah, in the Shefelah or lowland. (Joshua 15:40)
entries.definition_ko: 「사람의 담」이라는 뜻이니, 세펠라 곧 저지대에 있던 유다의 성읍 가운데 하나이다(여호수아 15:40).

entries.definition: (knotty), one of the towns from which Zubulun did not expel the Canaanites. (Judges 1:30) In the Talmud it is identified with “Zippori,” i.e. Sepphoris, now Seffurieh .
entries.definition_ko: 「마디진」이라는 뜻이니, 스불론이 가나안 사람을 쫓아내지 못한 성읍 가운데 하나이다(사사기 1:30). 탈무드는 이곳을 「시포리」 곧 세포리스와 같은 곳으로 보니 지금의 세푸리에이다.

entries.definition: Twice written in the Authorized Version for Chittim. (Genesis 10:4; 1 Chronicles 1:7)
entries.definition_ko: 흠정역이 깃딤을 이렇게 두 번 적은 꼴이다(창세기 10:4; 역대상 1:7).

entries.definition: [Bread]
entries.definition_ko: 떡 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: • The knives of the Egyptians, and of other nations in early times, were probably only of hard stone, and the use of the flint or stone knife was sometimes retained for sacred purposes after the introduction of iron and steel. • In their meals the Jews, like other Orientals, made little use of knives, but they were required both for slaughtering animals, either for food or sacrifice, and for cutting up the carcass. (Leviticus 7:33,34; 8:15,20,25; 9:13; Numbers 18:18; 1 Samuel 9:24) etc. • Smaller knives were in use for paring fruit (Josephus) and for sharpening pens. (Jeremiah 36:23) • The razor was often used for Nazarite purposes, for which a special chamber was reserved in the temple. (Numbers 6:5,9,19; Ezekiel 5:1), etc. • The pruning-hooks of (Isaiah 18:5) were probably curved knives. • The lancets of the priests of Baal were doubtless pointed knives. (1 Kings 18:28)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 애굽 사람과 다른 나라 사람들이 이른 때에 쓰던 칼은 아마 단단한 돌로만 만들었을 것이며, 쇠와 강철이 들어온 뒤에도 거룩한 일에는 부싯돌 곧 돌칼을 그대로 쓰기도 하였다. (2) 유대인은 다른 동방 사람처럼 밥상에서 칼을 거의 쓰지 않았으나, 먹으려고든 제사로든 짐승을 잡고 그 몸을 자르는 데에는 칼이 있어야 하였다(레위기 7:33,34; 레위기 8:15,20,25; 레위기 9:13; 민수기 18:18; 사무엘상 9:24 등). (3) 더 작은 칼은 과일을 깎거나(요세푸스) 붓을 깎는 데에 쓰였다(예레미야 36:23). (4) 삭도는 나실 사람의 일에 자주 쓰였으니, 그 일을 위하여 성전에 따로 방을 두었다(민수기 6:5,9,19; 에스겔 5:1 등). (5) 이사야 18:5의 낫은 아마 굽은 칼이었을 것이다. (6) 바알 선지자들의 칼날은 틀림없이 끝이 뾰족한 칼이었을 것이다(열왕기상 18:28).

entries.definition: a word employed in the Authorized Version to translate two terms which refer to some architectural or ornamental object, but which have nothing in common. • Caphtor .—This occurs in the description of the candlestick of the sacred tent in (Exodus 25:31-36) and Exod 37:17-22 • The second term, Peka’im, is found only in (1 Kings 6:18) and 1Kin 7:24The word no doubt signifies some globular thing resembling a small gourd or an egg, though as to the character of the ornament we are quite in the dark.
entries.definition_ko: 흠정역이 건축이나 꾸밈에 딸린 어떤 것을 가리키는 두 낱말을 옮기는 데 쓴 말이니, 이 두 낱말은 서로 아무 공통점이 없다. (1) 갑돌. 이것은 출애굽기 25:31-36과 출애굽기 37:17-22의 거룩한 장막의 등잔대를 적는 데에 나온다. (2) 둘째 낱말 페카임은 오직 열왕기상 6:18과 열왕기상 7:24에만 나온다. 이 말은 틀림없이 작은 박이나 알을 닮은 둥근 것을 뜻하겠으나, 그 꾸밈이 어떠하였는지는 우리가 전혀 알지 못한다.

entries.definition: (he-camel) is a word which occurs only in (Ezekiel 23:23) It may perhaps have been a city or district of Babylonia; or it may be a common noun, signifying “prince” or “nobleman.”
entries.definition_ko: 「수낙타」라는 뜻이니, 오직 에스겔 23:23에만 나오는 말이다. 아마 바벨론의 한 성이나 지역이었을 수도 있고, 「방백」이나 「귀인」을 뜻하는 보통 명사일 수도 있다.

entries.definition: (assembly), second of the three sons of Levi, from whom the three principal divisions of the Levites derived their origin and their name. (Genesis 46:11; Exodus 6:16) In the journeyings of the tabernacle of the sons of Kohath (Kohathites) had charge of the most holy portions of the vessels. (Numbers 4:1) ... Of the personal history of Kohath we know nothing, except that he came down to Egypt with Levi and Jacob, (Genesis 46:11) that his sister was Jochebed, (Exodus 6:20) and that he lived to the age of 133 years. (Exodus 6:18) (B.C. about 1491.)
entries.definition_ko: 「모임」이라는 뜻이니, 레위의 세 아들 가운데 둘째요 레위 사람의 세 큰 갈래가 그들에게서 그 뿌리와 이름을 얻었다(창세기 46:11; 출애굽기 6:16). 성막이 옮겨 다닐 때에 그핫 자손은 그 기구 가운데 가장 거룩한 것을 맡았다(민수기 4:1 이하). 그핫 개인의 역사에 대하여는, 레위와 야곱과 함께 애굽으로 내려간 것과(창세기 46:11) 요게벳이 그의 누이인 것과(출애굽기 6:20) 백삼십삼 세를 산 것 말고는 아는 바가 없다(출애굽기 6:18). (주전 1491년쯤.)

entries.definition: (voice of Jehovah). • A Benjamite whose descendants settled in Jerusalem after the return from the captivity. (Nehemiah 11:7) (B.C. before 536.) • The father of Ahab the false prophet, who was burnt by the king of Babylon. (Jeremiah 29:21) (B.C. before 594.)
entries.definition_ko: 「여호와의 소리」라는 뜻. (1) 베냐민 사람이니, 그 자손이 사로잡힘에서 돌아온 뒤에 예루살렘에 자리 잡았다(느헤미야 11:7). (주전 536년 이전.) (2) 거짓 선지자 아합의 아버지이니, 아합은 바벨론 왕에게 불살렸다(예레미야 29:21). (주전 594년 이전.)

entries.definition: (baldness). • Third son of Esau by Aholibamah. (Genesis 36:5,14,18; 1 Chronicles 1:35) He was born in Canaan before Esau migrated to Mount Seir, (Genesis 36:5-9) and was one of the “dukes” of Edom. (B.C. 1790.) • Another Edomitish “duke” of this name, sprung from Eliphaz, Esau’s son of Adah. (Genesis 36:16) • One of the “sons of Hebron,” in (1 Chronicles 2:43) • Son of Izhar the son of Kohath the son of Levi. He was leader of the famous rebellion against his cousins Moses and Aaron in the wilderness, for which he paid the penalty of perishing with his followers by an earthquake and flames of fire. (Numbers 16; 26:9-11) The particular grievance which rankled in the mind of Korah and his company was their exclusion from the office of the priesthood, and their being confined—those among them who were Levites— to the inferior service of the tabernacle. Korah’s position as leader in this rebellion was evidently the result of his personal character, which was that of a bold, haughty and ambitious man. (B.C. 1490.) In the New Testament (Jude 1:11) Korah is coupled with Cain and Balaam.
entries.definition_ko: 「대머리」라는 뜻. (1) 에서가 오홀리바마에게서 낳은 셋째 아들이다(창세기 36:5,14,18; 역대상 1:35). 그는 에서가 세일 산으로 옮기기 전에 가나안에서 태어났고(창세기 36:5-9) 에돔의 「족장」 가운데 하나였다. (주전 1790년.) (2) 이 이름을 지닌 또 다른 에돔 「족장」이니, 에서가 아다에게서 낳은 아들 엘리바스에게서 났다(창세기 36:16). (3) 역대상 2:43의 「헤브론의 아들들」 가운데 하나이다. (4) 레위의 아들 그핫의 아들 이스할의 아들이다. 그는 광야에서 사촌 모세와 아론을 거스른 저 이름난 반역을 이끌었고, 그 벌로 자기를 따르는 이들과 함께 땅이 갈라지고 불꽃이 이는 가운데 죽었다(민수기 16장; 민수기 26:9-11). 고라와 그 무리의 마음을 파고든 남다른 불만은 제사장 직분에서 제외된 것과, 그들 가운데 레위 사람들이 성막의 낮은 섬김에만 매인 것이었다. 이 반역에서 고라가 앞장선 것은 뚜렷이 그 됨됨이의 결과였으니, 그는 담대하고 거만하며 야심 있는 사람이었다. (주전 1490년.) 신약에서는 유다서 1:11이 고라를 가인과 발람과 나란히 든다.

entries.definition: (1 Chronicles 9:19,31) Kor’-hite, or Kor’athite, that portion of the Kohathites who were descended from Korah. They were an important branch of the singers, (2 Chronicles 20:19) hence we find eleven psalms (or twelve, if Psal 43is included under the same title as Psal 42, dedicated or assigned to the sons of Korah, viz., Psal 42,44-49,84,85,87,88,
entries.definition_ko: 역대상 9:19,31에 나오며 고라 사람 또는 고랏 사람이라고도 하니, 고핫 자손 가운데 고라에게서 난 이들이다. 그들은 노래하는 이들의 중요한 갈래였으니(역대하 20:19), 그래서 열한 편의 시가(시편 43편을 42편과 같은 표제 아래 넣으면 열두 편이) 고라 자손에게 바쳐지거나 그들에게 맡겨진 것을 본다. 곧 시편 42편, 44편부터 49편까지, 84편, 85편, 87편, 88편이다.

entries.definition: (partridge). • A Korahite, ancestor of Shallum and Meshelemiah, chief porters in the reign of David. (1 Chronicles 9:19; 26:1) (B.C. 1014.) • Son of Imnah, a Levite in the reign of Hezekiah. He had charge of the offerings. (2 Chronicles 31:14) (B.C. 726.) • In the Authorized Version of (1 Chronicles 26:19) “the sons of Kore” (following the Vulgate Core) should properly be “the sons of the Korhite.”
entries.definition_ko: 「자고새」라는 뜻. (1) 고라 사람이니, 다윗이 다스릴 때에 문지기의 우두머리였던 살룸과 므셀레먀의 조상이다(역대상 9:19; 역대상 26:1). (주전 1014년.) (2) 임나의 아들이니 히스기야가 다스릴 때의 레위 사람이다. 그는 예물을 맡았다(역대하 31:14). (주전 726년.) (3) 역대상 26:19의 흠정역에 나오는 「고레의 아들들」(불가타의 코레를 따른 것)은 마땅히 「고라 사람의 아들들」이라야 한다.

entries.definition: (thorn), (Ezra 2:61; Nehemiah 3:4,21) = Coz= Hakkoz.
entries.definition_ko: 「가시」라는 뜻이니(에스라 2:61; 느헤미야 3:4,21) 고스 곧 학고스와 같다.

entries.definition: (bow of Jehovah), the same as Kish or Kishi, the father of Ethan the Merarite. (1 Chronicles 15:17)
entries.definition_ko: 「여호와의 활」이라는 뜻이니, 기스 곧 기시와 같으며 므라리 사람 에단의 아버지이다(역대상 15:17).

entries.definition: (order), the son of Shelah and grandson of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:21)
entries.definition_ko: 「차례」라는 뜻이니, 셀라의 아들이요 유다의 손자이다(역대상 4:21).

entries.definition: (put in order). • An Ephraimite, ancestor of Joshua the son of Nun. (1 Chronicles 7:26) • The son of Gershom, elsewhere called Libni. (1 Chronicles 23:7,8,9; 26:21)
entries.definition_ko: 「차례대로 놓인」이라는 뜻. (1) 에브라임 사람이니 눈의 아들 여호수아의 조상이다(역대상 7:26). (2) 게르솜의 아들이니 다른 데에서는 립니라 부른다(역대상 23:7,8,9; 역대상 26:21).

entries.definition: (white). • Son of Bethuel, brother of Rebekah and father of Leah and Rachel. (B.C. about 18601740.) The elder branch of the family remained at Haran, Mesopotamia, when Abraham removed to the land of Canaan, and it is there that we first meet with Laban, as taking the leading part in the betrothal of his sister Rebekah to her cousin Isaac. (Genesis 24:10,29-60; 27:43; 29:5) The next time Laban appears in the sacred narrative it is as the host of his nephew Jacob at Haran. (Genesis 29:13,14) [Jacob] Jacob married Rachel and Leah, daughters of Laban, and remained with him 20 years, B.C. 1760-1740. But Laban’s dishonest and overreaching practice toward his nephew shows from what source Jacob inherited his tendency to sharp dealing. Nothing is said of Laban after Jacob left him. • One of the landmarks named in the obscure and disputed passage (1:1) The mention of Hezeroth has perhaps led to the only conjecture regarding Laban of which the writer is aware, namely, that it is identical with Libnah. (Numbers 33:20)
entries.definition_ko: 「흰」이라는 뜻. (1) 브두엘의 아들이요 리브가의 오라비이며 레아와 라헬의 아버지이다. (주전 1860~1740년쯤.) 아브라함이 가나안 땅으로 옮겨 갈 때에 이 집안의 손위 갈래는 메소보다미아 하란에 남았고, 우리가 라반을 처음 만나는 곳도 거기이니, 그가 누이 리브가를 사촌 이삭에게 시집보내는 일에 앞장선다(창세기 24:10,29-60; 창세기 27:43; 창세기 29:5). 라반이 성경 이야기에 다시 나타나는 것은 하란에서 조카 야곱을 맞아들이는 이로서이다(창세기 29:13,14). 야곱 항목을 보라. 야곱은 라반의 딸 라헬과 레아와 혼인하여 주전 1760년부터 1740년까지 스무 해를 그와 함께 지냈다. 그러나 라반이 조카를 대하여 정직하지 못하고 속임수를 쓴 것을 보면 야곱이 약삭빠르게 거래하는 성향을 어디서 물려받았는지 알 수 있다. 야곱이 그를 떠난 뒤로 라반에 대하여는 말한 것이 없다. (2) 뜻이 흐리고 다투어지는 신명기 1:1에 이름이 오른 표지 가운데 하나이다. 하세롯이 언급된 데서 아마 라반에 대한, 글쓴이가 아는 유일한 짐작이 나왔을 것이니, 곧 이곳이 립나와 같다는 것이다(민수기 33:20).

entries.definition: in Greece the inhabitants of Sparta or Lacedaemon, with whom the Jews claimed kindred. 1 Macc. 12:2,5,6,20,21; 14:20,23; 15:23; 2 Macc. 5:9.
entries.definition_ko: 헬라의 스파르타 곧 라게데몬 사람이니, 유대인이 그들과 겨레붙이라 주장하였다. 마카베오상 12:2,5,6,20,21; 14:20,23; 15:23과 마카베오하 5:9에 나온다.

entries.definition: the thong or fastening by which the sandal was attached to the foot. It occurs int he proverbial expression in (Genesis 14:23) and is there used to denote something trivial or worthless. Another semi-proverbial expression in (Luke 3:16) points to the fact that the office of bearing and unfastening the shoes of great personages fell to the meanest slaves.
entries.definition_ko: 신을 발에 매는 끈 또는 매는 것이다. 창세기 14:23의 속담 같은 말에 나오며 거기서는 하찮거나 값없는 것을 나타내는 데 쓰인다. 누가복음 3:16의 또 다른 속담 같은 말은, 높은 이의 신을 들고 그 끈을 푸는 일이 가장 낮은 종에게 돌아갔다는 사실을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: (invincible), a city lying south of Jerusalem, on the borders of Simeon, and belonging to the Amorites, the king of which joined with four others, at the invitation of Adonizedek king of Jerusalem, to chastise the Gibeonites for their league with Israel. (Joshua 10:3,5) They were routed by Joshua at Beth-horon, and the king of Lachish fell a victim with the others under the trees at Makkedah. ver. (Joshua 10:26) The destruction of the town shortly followed the death of the king. vs. (Joshua 10:31-33) In the special statement that the attack lasted two days, in contradistinction to the other cities which were taken in one (see ver. 35), we gain our first glimpse of that strength of position for which Lachish was afterward remarkable. Lachish was one of the cities fortified and garrisoned by Rehoboam after the revolt of the northern kingdom. (2 Chronicles 11:9) In the reign of Hezekiah it was one of the cities taken by Sennacherib. This siege is considered by Layard and Hincks to be depicted on the slabs found by the former in one of the chambers of the palace at Kouyunjik. After the return from captivity, Lachish with its surrounding “fields” was reoccupied by the Jews. (Nehemiah 11:30)
entries.definition_ko: 「칠 수 없는」이라는 뜻이니, 예루살렘 남쪽 시므온 어귀에 있던 성이요 아모리 사람의 것이었다. 그 왕이 예루살렘 왕 아도니세덱의 부름을 받아 다른 넷과 함께 기브온이 이스라엘과 동맹한 일로 그들을 벌하려 하였다(여호수아 10:3,5). 그들은 벧호론에서 여호수아에게 패주하였고, 라기스 왕도 다른 왕들과 함께 막게다의 나무 아래에서 죽임을 당하였다(여호수아 10:26). 그 왕이 죽은 뒤에 얼마 안 되어 그 성읍도 헐렸다(여호수아 10:31-33). 다른 성읍은 하루 만에 빼앗았는데(여호수아 10:35를 보라) 이곳을 치는 데에는 이틀이 걸렸다는 남다른 기록에서, 우리는 라기스가 뒤에 이름난 그 자리의 튼튼함을 처음으로 엿본다. 라기스는 북쪽 나라가 갈라져 나간 뒤에 르호보암이 굳게 하고 군사를 둔 성읍 가운데 하나였다(역대하 11:9). 히스기야가 다스릴 때에 산헤립이 빼앗은 성읍 가운데 하나였다. 이 에워쌈이 레이어드가 쿠윤지크 궁궐의 한 방에서 찾아낸 석판에 새겨져 있다고 레이어드와 힝크스는 본다. 사로잡힘에서 돌아온 뒤에 유대인이 라기스와 그 둘레 「밭」에 다시 들어가 살았다(느헤미야 11:30).

entries.definition: (of God), the father of Eliasaph. (Numbers 3:24)
entries.definition_ko: 「하나님께 속한」이라는 뜻이니, 엘리아삽의 아버지이다(민수기 3:24).

entries.definition: (oppression), son of Jahath, one of the descendants of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:2)
entries.definition_ko: 「누름」이라는 뜻이니, 야핫의 아들이요 유다의 후손 가운데 하나이다(역대상 4:2).

entries.definition: (well of the living God), The well. In this form is given in the Authorized Version of (Genesis 24:62) and Genesis25:11 The name of the famous well of Hagar’s relief, in the oasis of verdure round which Isaac afterward resided. It was southwest of Beersheba.
entries.definition_ko: 「살아 계신 하나님의 우물」이라는 뜻이니, 흠정역이 창세기 24:62와 창세기 25:11에서 이 꼴로 적은 이름이다. 하갈이 도움을 얻은 저 이름난 우물이요, 그 둘레 푸른 오아시스에 뒤에 이삭이 살았다. 브엘세바 남서쪽에 있었다.

entries.definition: (provisions), a town in the lowland district of Judah. (Joshua 15:40)
entries.definition_ko: 「양식」이라는 뜻이니, 유다 저지대에 있던 성읍이다(여호수아 15:40).

entries.definition: (warrior), the brother of Goliath the Gittite, slain by Elhanan the son of Zair or Zaor. (1 Chronicles 20:5) (B.C. 1020.)
entries.definition_ko:
「용사」라는 뜻이니, 가드 사람 골리앗의 아우요 야일의 아들 엘하난에게 죽임을 당하였다(역대상 20:5). (주전 1020년.)
※ 원문 훼손: Zair or Zaor → Jair(야일)로 보임
※ 판정 근거: CCEL 훼손. 「Zair or Zaor」는 「Jair」(야일)의 훼손으로 보인다. 라흐미는 야일의 아들 엘하난이 죽인 골리앗의 아우이다. 2018년 CCEL 전자판에도 같은 자리에서 같은 꼴로 있으므로 우리 쪽 추출 훼손이 아니다. 다만 이 PDF는 CCEL이 찍어 낸 전자판이요 인쇄본 스캔이 아니므로, 인쇄본에도 그러하였는지는 이 파일로 가릴 수 없다.

entries.definition: (lion), father of Phaltiel, to whom Saul had given Michal, David’s wife. (1 Samuel 25:44; 2 Samuel 3:15)
entries.definition_ko: 「사자」라는 뜻이니, 발디엘의 아버지이다. 사울이 다윗의 아내 미갈을 발디엘에게 주었다(사무엘상 25:44; 사무엘하 3:15).

entries.definition: [Palestina And Palestine]
entries.definition_ko: 팔레스타인 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: (fortification), properly formed the landmarks of the boundary of Naphtali. (Joshua 19:33)
entries.definition_ko: 「요새」라는 뜻이니, 납달리의 경계를 나타내는 곳 가운데 하나이다(여호수아 19:33).

entries.definition: are the young of sheep, but originally included also the young of goats. They formed an important part of almost every sacrifice. (Exodus 29:38-41; Numbers 28:9,11; 29,13-40) etc. [On the paschal lamb see Passover]
entries.definition_ko: 양의 새끼이나 본디 염소의 새끼도 아울렀다. 거의 모든 제사에서 중요한 몫을 이루었다(출애굽기 29:38-41; 민수기 28:9,11; 민수기 29:13-40 등). 유월절 어린양에 대하여는 유월절 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: (powerful), properly Lemech. • The fifth lineal descendant from Cain. (Genesis 4:18-24) He is the only one except Enoch, of the posterity of Cain, whose history is related with some detail. His two wives, Adah and Zillah, and his daughter Naamah, are, with Eve, the only antediluvian women whose names are mentioned by Moses. His three sons, Jabal, Jubal and Tubal-cain, are celebrated in Scripture as authors of useful inventions. The remarkable poem which Lamech uttered may perhaps be regarded as Lamech’s son of exultation on the invention of the sword by his son Tubal-cain, in the possession of which he foresaw a great advantage to himself and his family over any enemies. • The father of Noah. (Genesis 5:29)
entries.definition_ko: 「힘 있는」이라는 뜻이니 본디 레멕이다. (1) 가인에게서 다섯째로 이어 내려온 후손이다(창세기 4:18-24). 가인의 자손 가운데 에녹을 빼고 그 역사가 얼마쯤 자세히 적힌 이는 그뿐이다. 그의 두 아내 아다와 씰라와 그 딸 나아마는 하와와 아울러 모세가 이름을 든 홍수 이전의 유일한 여인들이다. 그 세 아들 야발과 유발과 두발가인은 쓸모 있는 것을 지어낸 이들로 성경에 이름이 높다. 라멕이 읊은 저 남다른 시는 아마 그 아들 두발가인이 칼을 지어낸 일을 두고 라멕이 뽐내어 부른 노래로 볼 수 있으니, 그것을 지님으로 자기와 제 집안이 어떤 원수보다 크게 유리하리라 내다본 것이다. (2) 노아의 아버지이다(창세기 5:29).

entries.definition: Title.—The Hebrew title of this book, Ecah, is taken, like the titles of the five books of Moses, from the Hebrew word with which it opens. Author.—The poems included in this collection appear in the Hebrew canon with no name attached to them, but Jeremiah has been almost universally regarded as their author. Date.—The poems belong unmistakably to the last days of the kingdom, or the commencement of the exile, B.C. 629-586. They are written by one who speaks, with the vividness and intensity of an eye-witness, of the misery which he bewails. Contents.—The book consists of five chapter, each of which, however, is a separate poem, complete in itself, and having a distinct subject, but brought at the same time under a plan which includes them all. A complicated alphabetic structure pervades nearly the whole book. (1) Chs. 1,2 and 4 contain twenty-two verses each, arranged in alphabetic order, each verse falling into three nearly balanced clauses; ch. (Lamentations 2:19) forms an exception, as having a fourth clause. (2) Ch. 3 contains three short verses under each letter of the alphabet, the initial letter being three times repeated. (3) Ch. 5 contains the same number of verses as chs. 1,2,4, but without the alphabetic order. Jeremiah was not merely a patriotpoet, weeping over the ruin of his country; he was a prophet who had seen all this coming, and had foretold it as inevitable. There are perhaps few portions of the Old Testament which appear to have done the work they were meant to do more effectually than this. The book has supplied thousands with the fullest utterance for their sorrows in the critical periods of national or individual suffering. We may well believe that it soothed the weary years of the Babylonian exile. It enters largely into the order of the Latin Church for the services of passion-week. On the ninth day of the month of Ab (July-August), the Lamentations of Jeremiah were read, year by year, with fasting and weeping, to commemorate the misery out of which the people had been delivered.
entries.definition_ko: 제목. 이 책의 히브리 제목 에카는 모세 오경의 제목들처럼 그 첫머리에 오는 히브리 낱말에서 왔다. 지은이. 이 모음에 든 시들은 히브리 정경에 이름이 붙지 않은 채 나오나, 예레미야가 그 지은이로 거의 두루 여겨져 왔다. 때. 이 시들은 틀림없이 이 나라의 마지막 날이나 사로잡힘이 시작될 때, 곧 주전 629년부터 586년 사이에 속한다. 눈으로 본 이의 생생함과 뜨거움으로 자기가 슬퍼하는 그 비참함을 말하는 이가 쓴 것이다. 내용. 이 책은 다섯 장으로 이루어지나 각 장이 저마다 온전한 따로 된 시요 저마다 다른 주제를 지니면서도, 동시에 그 모두를 아우르는 짜임 아래 놓여 있다. 얽힌 자모 순서의 짜임이 거의 온 책에 배어 있다. (1) 1장과 2장과 4장은 저마다 스물두 절을 담고 자모 순서로 벌여 놓았으며, 각 절이 거의 고른 세 마디로 나뉜다. 다만 예레미야애가 2:19는 넷째 마디가 있어 예외이다. (2) 3장은 자모의 글자마다 세 짧은 절을 담고 그 첫 글자를 세 번씩 되풀이한다. (3) 5장은 1장과 2장과 4장과 같은 수의 절을 담으나 자모 순서를 따르지 않는다. 예레미야는 다만 제 나라의 무너짐을 슬퍼한 나라 사랑의 시인만이 아니었다. 그는 이 모든 것이 오는 것을 미리 보고 그것이 피할 수 없음을 미리 말한 선지자였다. 구약에서 마땅히 할 일을 이 책보다 더 잘 이룬 부분은 아마 드물 것이다. 이 책은 나라나 개인이 고난을 겪는 위태로운 때에 수많은 이에게 그 슬픔을 온전히 쏟아 낼 말을 주었다. 이 책이 바벨론 사로잡힘의 고단한 세월을 달래었으리라 넉넉히 믿을 만하다. 라틴 교회의 고난 주간 예배 순서에도 크게 들어가 있다. 아브월(칠팔월) 아흐레에는 예레미야애가를 해마다 금식하며 울며 읽어, 그 백성이 건짐받아 나온 그 비참함을 기렸다.

entries.definition: • That part of the golden candlestick belonging to the tabernacle which bore the light; also of each of the ten candlesticks placed by Solomon in the temple before the holy of holies. (Exodus 25:37; 1 Kings 7:49; 2 Chronicles 4:20; 13:11; Zechariah 4:2) The lamps were lighted every evening and cleansed every morning. (Exodus 30:7,8) • A torch or flambeau, such as was carried by the soldiers of Gideon. (Judges 7:16,20) comp. Judg 15:4The use in marriage processions of lamps fed with oil is alluded to in the parable of the ten virgins. (Matthew 25:1) Modern Egyptian lamps consist of small glass vessels with a tube at the bottom containing a cotton wick twisted around a piece of straw. For night travelling, a lantern composed of waxed cloth strained over a sort of cylinder of wire rings, and a top and bottom of perforated copper. This would, in form at least, answer to the lamps within pitchers of Gideon. “The Hebrews, like the ancient Greeks and Romans, as well as the modern Orientals, were accustomed to burn lamps all night. This custom, with the effect produced by their going out or being extinguished, supplies various figures to the sacred writers. (2 Samuel 21:17; Proverbs 13:9; 20:20) On the other hand, the keeping up of a lamp’s light is used as a symbol of enduring and unbroken succession. (1 Kings 11:36; 15:4; Psalms 132:17) ”—McClintock and Strong.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 성막에 딸린 금 등잔대에서 불을 지니는 부분이니, 솔로몬이 성전 지성소 앞에 놓은 열 등잔대의 각 부분도 그러하다(출애굽기 25:37; 열왕기상 7:49; 역대하 4:20; 역대하 13:11; 스가랴 4:2). 등불은 저녁마다 켜고 아침마다 손질하였다(출애굽기 30:7,8). (2) 기드온의 군사들이 든 것과 같은 횃불이다(사사기 7:16,20; 사사기 15:4와 견주라). 혼인 행렬에 기름을 넣은 등을 쓴 일이 열 처녀 비유에 비쳐 있다(마태복음 25:1). 오늘 애굽의 등은 밑에 관이 달린 작은 유리 그릇으로 되어 있고, 그 관 안에 짚 조각을 감은 무명 심지가 있다. 밤길에는 쇠 고리로 된 둥근 틀에 밀 먹인 천을 씌우고 위아래를 구멍 뚫은 구리로 막은 초롱을 쓴다. 이것은 적어도 그 모양에서는 기드온의 항아리 안에 든 등에 들어맞을 것이다. 「히브리 사람은 옛 헬라 사람과 로마 사람처럼, 또 오늘 동방 사람처럼 밤새 등을 켜 두는 버릇이 있었다. 이 버릇과 등이 꺼지거나 꺼뜨려질 때의 결과가 성경 기자들에게 여러 비유를 준다(사무엘하 21:17; 잠언 13:9; 잠언 20:20). 다른 한편으로 등불을 계속 켜 두는 일은 끊이지 않고 이어짐의 상징으로 쓰인다(열왕기상 11:36; 열왕기상 15:4; 시편 132:17).」—매클린톡과 스트롱.

entries.definition: This word is found in (1 Kings 18:28) only. The Hebrew term is romach, which is elsewhere rendered, and appears to mean a javelin or light spear. In the original edition of the Authorized Version (1611) the word is “lancers.”
entries.definition_ko: 이 말은 오직 열왕기상 18:28에만 나온다. 히브리 낱말은 로마흐이니 다른 데에서 옮겨진 대로 창 또는 가벼운 창을 뜻하는 듯하다. 흠정역 초판(1611년)에는 이 말이 「랜서스」로 되어 있다.

entries.definition: (so called of its shining) occurs only in (John 18:3) (It there probably denotes any kind of covered light, in distinction from a simple taper or common house-light, as well as from a flambeau. Lanterns were much employed by the Romans in military operations. Two, of bronze, have been found among the ruins of Herculaneum and Pompeii. They are cylindrical, with translucent horn sides, the lamp within being furnished with an extinguisher.—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: (빛난다 하여 그렇게 부르는 것이니) 오직 요한복음 18:3에만 나온다. (여기서는 아마 그저 초나 여느 집안 등불과 다르고 횃불과도 다른, 무엇으로 덮은 온갖 등을 가리킬 것이다. 초롱은 로마 사람이 싸움에 많이 썼다. 청동으로 만든 것 둘이 헤르쿨라네움과 폼페이의 폐허에서 나왔다. 그것들은 둥근 통 모양이요 옆이 비치는 뿔로 되어 있으며, 그 안의 등에는 불을 끄는 덮개가 달려 있다.—편집자)

entries.definition: (justice of the people), a town in the Roman province of Asia situated in the valley of the Maeander, on a small river called the Lycus, with Colossae and Hierapolis a few miles distant to the west. Built, or rather rebuilt, by one of the Seleucid monarchs, and named in honor of his wife, Laodicea became under the Roman government a place of some importance. Its trade was considerable; it lay on the line of a great road; and it was the seat of a conventus . From the third chapter and seventeenth verse of Revelation we should gather it was a place of great wealth. Christianity was introduced into Laodicea, not, however, as it would seem, through the direct agency of St. Paul. We have good reason for believing that when, in writing from Rome to the Christians of Colossae, he sent a greeting to those of Laodicea, he had not personally visited either place. But the preaching of the gospel at Ephesus, (Acts 18:19; Acts 19:41) must inevitably have resulted in the formation of churches in the neighboring cities, especially where Jews were settled; and there were Jews in Laodicea. In subsequent times it became a Christian city of eminence, the see of bishop and a meeting-place of councils. The Mohammedan invaders destroyed it, and it is now a scene of utter desolation, as was prophesied in (Revelation 3:14-22) and the extensive ruins near Denislu justify all that we read of Laodicea in Greek and Roman writers. Another biblical subject of interest is connected with Laodicea. From (Colossians 4:16) it appears that St. Paul wrote a letter to this place when he wrote the letter to Colossae. Ussher’s view is that it was the same as the Epistle to the Ephesians, which was a circular letter sent to Laodicea among other places. The apocryphal Epistola ad Laodicenses is a late and clumsy forgery.
entries.definition_ko: 「백성의 정의」라는 뜻이니, 로마의 아시아 도에 있던 성읍이요 마이안데르 골짜기의 리쿠스라는 작은 강가에 자리 잡았고, 서쪽으로 몇 마일 떨어져 골로새와 히에라볼리가 있었다. 셀레우코스 왕가의 한 임금이 세웠으니, 더 바르게는 다시 세워 제 아내를 기려 이름을 붙였고, 로마의 다스림 아래에서 라오디게아는 얼마쯤 중요한 곳이 되었다. 그 장사가 상당하였고 큰길 위에 자리 잡았으며 재판구의 중심이었다. 요한계시록 3장 17절에서 우리는 이곳이 큰 부를 지닌 곳이었음을 알 수 있다. 그리스도교가 라오디게아에 들어왔으나 사도 바울이 몸소 한 일로 보이지는 않는다. 그가 로마에서 골로새의 그리스도인에게 편지하면서 라오디게아의 그리스도인에게 문안한 것을 보면, 그가 두 곳 어느 쪽도 몸소 찾아가지 않았다고 믿을 만한 좋은 까닭이 있다. 그러나 에베소에서 복음을 전한 일이(사도행전 18:19; 사도행전 19:41) 이웃 성읍들, 특히 유대인이 자리 잡은 곳에 교회가 세워지는 열매를 맺지 않을 수 없었고, 라오디게아에도 유대인이 있었다. 뒤에 이곳은 이름난 그리스도교의 성이 되어 주교좌가 있었고 공의회가 모이는 곳이었다. 회교의 침략자들이 이곳을 헐어, 요한계시록 3:14-22이 미리 말한 대로 이제는 온통 황폐한 자리이며, 데니슬루 가까이의 넓은 폐허가 헬라와 로마 저술가들이 라오디게아를 두고 말한 모든 것을 뒷받침한다. 성경에 관한 또 하나의 흥미로운 주제가 라오디게아와 이어져 있다. 골로새서 4:16에서 사도 바울이 골로새에 편지할 때에 이곳에도 편지하였음이 드러난다. 어셔는 그것이 에베소서와 같은 것이니, 에베소서가 라오디게아를 비롯한 여러 곳에 돌려 보낸 편지였다고 본다. 외경 「라오디게아인에게 보낸 편지」는 뒷날의 서투른 위작이다.

entries.definition: the inhabitants of Laodicea. (Colossians 4:16; Revelation 3:14)
entries.definition_ko: 라오디게아 사람들이다(골로새서 4:16; 요한계시록 3:14).

entries.definition: (torches), the inhabitants of Laodicea. (Colossians 4:16; Revelation 3:14)
entries.definition_ko:
「횃불」이라는 뜻이다.
※ 원문 오류: 이 항목의 뜻풀이 자리에 앞의 「라오디게아 사람들」 항목의 글이 잘못 들어가 있음. 라비돗은 사사기 4:4의 드보라의 남편 이름이다
※ 판정 근거: CCEL 훼손. 이 항목의 뜻풀이 자리에 앞의 「라오디게아 사람들」 항목의 글이 그대로 들어가 있다. 라비돗은 사사기 4:4의 「랍비돗의 아내 여선지자 드보라」에 나오는 드보라의 남편 이름이다. 2018년 CCEL 전자판에도 같은 자리에서 같은 꼴로 있으므로 우리 쪽 추출 훼손이 아니다. 다만 이 PDF는 CCEL이 찍어 낸 전자판이요 인쇄본 스캔이 아니므로, 인쇄본에도 그러하였는지는 이 파일로 가릴 수 없다.

entries.definition: (Heb. duciphath) occurs only in (Leviticus 11:19) and in the parallel passage of (14:18) amongst the list of those birds which were forbidden by the law of Moses to be eaten by the Israelites. Commentators generally agree that the hoopoe is the bird intended. The hoopoe is an occasional visitor to England, arriving for the most part in the autumn. Its crest is very elegant; each of the long feathers forming it is tipped with black.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리 말로 두키팟이니, 오직 레위기 11:19와 그 나란한 대목인 신명기 14:18에만 나오며, 모세의 율법이 이스라엘 사람에게 먹지 못하게 한 새들의 명단에 든다. 주석하는 이들은 대체로 이것이 후투티라는 데에 뜻을 같이한다. 후투티는 이따금 영국을 찾아오는데 대개 가을에 온다. 그 볏은 매우 우아하니, 그것을 이루는 긴 깃털마다 끝이 검다.

entries.definition: (Acts 27:8) a city of Crete, the ruins of which were discovered in 1856, a few miles to the eastward of Fair Havens.
entries.definition_ko: 사도행전 27:8에 나오니, 그레데의 한 성이요 그 폐허가 1856년에 미항 동쪽 몇 마일 되는 곳에서 발견되었다.

entries.definition: (fissure), a place noticed in (Genesis 10:19) as marking the limit of the country of the Canaanites. It lay somewhere in the southeast of Palestine. Jerome and other writers identify it with Callirrhoe, a spot famous for hot springs, near the eastern shore of the Dead Sea.
entries.definition_ko: 「갈라진 틈」이라는 뜻이니, 창세기 10:19에 가나안 사람의 땅 경계를 나타내는 곳으로 나온다. 팔레스타인 남동쪽 어딘가에 있었다. 제롬을 비롯한 여러 저술가는 이곳을 칼리로에와 같은 곳으로 보니, 이는 사해 동쪽 기슭 가까이 온천으로 이름난 곳이다.

entries.definition: (the plain), one of the Canaanite towns whose kings were killed by Joshua. (Joshua 12:18)
entries.definition_ko: 「그 평지」라는 뜻이니, 여호수아가 그 왕들을 죽인 가나안 성읍 가운데 하나이다(여호수아 12:18).

entries.definition: the language spoken by the Romans, is mentioned only in (John 19:20) and Luke 23:38
entries.definition_ko: 로마 사람이 쓰던 말이니, 오직 요한복음 19:20과 누가복음 23:38에만 언급된다.

entries.definition: this word is used for a latticed window or simply a network placed before a window or balcony. Perhaps the network through which Ahaziah fell and received his mortal injury was on the parapet of his palace. (2 Kings 1:2) (The latticed window is much used in warm eastern countries. It frequently projects from the wall (like our bay windows), and is formed of reticulated work, often highly ornamental, portions of which are hinged so that they may be opened or shut at pleasure. The object is to keep the apartments cool by intercepting the direct rays of the sun, while the air is permitted to circulate freely.—Fairbairn. [See Houseand Window]
entries.definition_ko: 이 말은 격자 창이나 창 또는 난간 앞에 놓은 그물 짜임을 가리킨다. 아하시야가 떨어져 죽을 상처를 입은 그 그물은 아마 그 궁궐 난간에 있었을 것이다(열왕기하 1:2). (격자 창은 더운 동방 나라에서 많이 쓴다. 흔히 담에서 내밀어 있고(우리의 내닫이창처럼) 그물처럼 얽은 짜임으로 되어 있으며 흔히 매우 곱게 꾸며져 있는데, 그 얼마는 돌쩌귀를 달아 뜻대로 열고 닫을 수 있다. 햇빛이 곧바로 드는 것을 막아 방을 시원하게 하면서도 바람은 마음껏 드나들게 하려는 것이다.—페어베언.) 집 항목과 창 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: • In the tabernacle, a vessel of brass containing water for the priests to wash their hands and feet before offering sacrifice. It stood in the fore offering sacrifice. It stood in the court between the altar and the door of the tabernacle. (Exodus 30:19,21) It rested on a basis, i.e. a foot, which, was well as the laver itself, was made from the mirrors of the women who assembled at the door of the tabernacle court. (Exodus 38:8) The form of the laver is not specified, but may be assumed to have been circular. Like the other vessels belonging to the tabernacle, it was, together with its “foot,” consecrated with oil. (Leviticus 8:10,11) • In Solomon’s temple, besides the great molten sea, there were ten lavers of brass, raised on bases, (1 Kings 7:27,39) five on the north and five on the south side of the court of the priests. They were used for washing the animals to be offered in burnt offerings. (2 Chronicles 4:6)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 성막에서는 제사장이 제사를 드리기 전에 손과 발을 씻을 물을 담은 놋 그릇이었다. 그것은 제사를 드리는 자리 앞에 놓였으니, 곧 제단과 성막 문 사이의 뜰에 놓였다(출애굽기 30:19,21). 받침 곧 발 위에 놓였는데, 그 받침도 물두멍 자체도 성막 뜰 문에 모인 여인들의 거울로 만들었다(출애굽기 38:8). 물두멍의 모양은 밝혀져 있지 않으나 둥글었으리라 볼 수 있다. 성막에 딸린 다른 기구들처럼 이것도 그 「발」과 함께 기름으로 거룩히 구별되었다(레위기 8:10,11). (2) 솔로몬의 성전에는 큰 놋 바다 말고도 받침 위에 얹은 놋 물두멍 열이 있었으니(열왕기상 7:27,39), 제사장의 뜰 북쪽에 다섯, 남쪽에 다섯이었다. 번제로 드릴 짐승을 씻는 데에 썼다(역대하 4:6).

entries.definition: The word is properly used, in Scripture as elsewhere, to express a definite commandment laid down by any recognized authority; but when the word is used with the article, and without any words of limitation, it refers to the expressed will to God, and in nine cases out of ten to the Mosaic law, or to the Pentateuch of which it forms the chief portion. The Hebrew word torah (law) lays more stress on its moral authority, as teaching the truth and guiding in the right way; the Greek nomos (law), on its constraining power as imposed and enforced by a recognized authority. The sense of the word, however, extends its scope and assumes a more abstracts character in the writings of St. Paul. Nomos, when used by him with the article, still refers in general to the law of Moses; but when used without the article, so as to embrace any manifestation of “law,” it includes all powers which act on the will of man by compulsion, or by the pressure of external motives, whether their commands be or be not expressed in definite forms. The occasional use of the word “law” (as in (Romans 3:27) “law of faith”) to denote an internal principle of action does not really mitigate against the general rule. It should also be noticed that the title “the Law” is occasionally used loosely to refer to the whole of the Old Testament, as in (John 10:34) referring to (Psalms 82:6) in (John 15:25) referring to (Psalms 35:19) and in (1 Corinthians 14:21) referring to (Isaiah 28:11,12)
entries.definition_ko: 이 말은 성경에서도 다른 데에서와 같이 인정받은 권위가 정한 뚜렷한 명령을 나타내는 데에 바르게 쓰인다. 그러나 이 말이 관사와 함께, 그리고 아무 한정하는 말 없이 쓰이면 하나님의 드러내신 뜻을 가리키며, 열에 아홉은 모세의 율법이나 그것이 큰 부분을 이루는 모세 오경을 가리킨다. 히브리 낱말 토라는 진리를 가르치고 바른 길로 이끈다는 그 도덕의 권위에 더 무게를 둔다. 헬라 말 노모스는 인정받은 권위가 지우고 시행한다는 그 매어 두는 힘에 무게를 둔다. 그러나 이 말의 뜻은 사도 바울의 글에서 그 범위가 넓어지고 더 추상하는 성격을 띤다. 그가 관사와 함께 노모스를 쓸 때에는 여전히 대체로 모세의 율법을 가리키나, 관사 없이 써서 「법」이 나타나는 모든 것을 아우를 때에는, 그 명령이 뚜렷한 꼴로 밝혀졌든 아니든 사람의 뜻에 강제로 또는 바깥 동기의 눌림으로 작용하는 모든 힘을 아우른다. 「법」이라는 말이 이따금 속에서 일어나는 행함의 원리를 나타내는 데 쓰이는 것은(로마서 3:27의 「믿음의 법」처럼) 이 두루 통하는 규칙에 참으로 어긋나지 않는다. 또한 「그 율법」이라는 이름이 이따금 느슨하게 구약 전체를 가리키는 데 쓰인다는 점도 눈여겨보아야 하니, 요한복음 10:34가 시편 82:6을 가리키고, 요한복음 15:25가 시편 35:19를 가리키며, 고린도전서 14:21이 이사야 28:11,12를 가리키는 것이 그러하다.

entries.definition: It will be the object of this article to give a brief analysis of the substance of this law, to point out its main principles, and to explain the position which it occupies in the progress of divine revelation. In order to do this the more clearly, it seems best to speak of the law, 1st. In relation to the past; 2d. In its own intrinsic character. • (a) In reference to the past, it is all-important, for the proper understanding of the law, to remember its entire dependence on the Abrahamic covenant. See (Galatians 3:17-24) That covenant had a twofold character. It contained the “spiritual promise” of the Messiah; but it contained also the temporal promises subsidiary to the former. (b) The nature of this relation of the law to the promise is clearly pointed out. The belief in God as the Redeemer of man, and the hope of his manifestation as such int he person of the Messiah, involved the belief that the Spiritual Power must be superior to all carnal obstructions, and that there was in man spiritual element which could rule his life by communion with a spirit from above. But it involved also the idea of an antagonistic power of evil, from which man was to be redeemed, existing in each individual, and existing also in the world at large. (c) Nor is it less essential to remark the period of the history at which it was given. It marked and determined the transition of Israel from the condition of a tribe to that of a nation, and its definite assumption of a distinct position and office in the history of the world. (d) Yet, though new in its general conception, it was probably not wholly new in its materials. There must necessarily have been, before the law, commandments and revelations of a fragmentary character, under which Israel had hitherto grown up. So far therefore as they were consistent with the objects of the Jewish law, the customs of Palestine and the laws of Egypt would doubtless be traceable in the Mosaic system. (e) In close connection with, and almost in consequence of, this reference to antiquity, we find an accommodation of the law to the temper and circumstances of the Israelites, to which our Lord refers int he case of divorce, (Matthew 19:7,8) as necessarily interfering with its absolute perfection. In many cases it rather should be said to guide and modify existing usages than actually to sanction them; and the ignorance of their existence may lead to a conception of its ordinances not only erroneous, but actually the reverse of the truth. (f) In close connection with this subject we observe also the gradual process by which the law was revealed to the Israelites. In Ex 20-23, in direct connection with the revelation from Mount Sinai, that which may be called the rough outline of the Mosaic law is given by God, solemnly recorded by Moses, and accepted by the people. In Ex 25-31, there is a similar outline of the Mosaic ceremonial. On the basis of these it may be conceived that the fabric of the Mosaic system gradually grew up under the requirements of the time. The first revelation of the law in anything like a perfect form is found in the book of Deuteronomy. yet even then the revelation was not final; it was the duty of the prophets to amend and explain it in special points, (Ezekiel 18:1) ... and to bring out more clearly its great principles. • In giving an analysis of the substance of the law, it will probably be better to treat it, as any other system of laws is usually treated, by dividing it into— I. Laws Civil; II. Laws Criminal: III. Laws Judicial and Constitutional; IV. Laws Ecclesiastical and Ceremonial. I. LAWS CIVIL. • LAW OF PERSonS. (a) FatherAND Son.—the power of a father to be held sacred; cursing or smiting, (Exodus 21:15,17; Leviticus 20:9) and stubborn and willful disobedience, to be considered capital crimes. But uncontrolled power of life and death was apparently refused to the father, and vested only in the congregation. (21:1821) Right of the first-born to a double portion of the inheritance not to be set aside by partiality. (21:15-17) Inheritance by daughters to be allowed in default of sons, provided, (Numbers 27:6-8) comp. Numb 36:1... that heiresses married in their own tribe. Daughters unmarried to be entirely dependent on their father. (Numbers 30:3-5) (b) HusbandAND Wife.—the power of a husband to be so great that a wife could never be sui juris, or enter independently into any engagement, even before God. (Numbers 30:6-15) A widow or a divorced wife became independent, and did not against fall under her father’s power. ver. (Numbers 30:9) Divorce (for uncleanness) allowed, but to be formal and irrevocable. (24:1-4) Marriage within certain degrees forbidden. (Leviticus 18:1) ... etc. A slave wife, whether bought or captive, not to be actual property, nor to be sold; if illtreated, to be ipso facto free. (Exodus 21:7-9; 21:10-14) Slander against a wife’s virginity to be punished by fine, and by deprived of power of divorce; on the other hand, ante-connubial uncleanness in her to be punished by death. (22:13-21) the raising up of seed (Levirate law) a formal right to be claimed by the widow, under pain of infamy, with a view to preservation of families. (25:5-10) (c) MASTER AND Slave.—Power of master so far limited that death under actual chastisement was punishable, (Exodus 21:20) and maiming was to give liberty ipso facto . vs. (Exodus 21:26,27) The Hebrew slave to be freed at the sabbatical year, and provided with necessaries (his wife and children to go with only if they came to his master with him), unless by his own formal act he consented to be a perpetual slave. (Exodus 21:1-6; 15:12-18) In any case, it would seem, to be freed at the jubilee, (Leviticus 25:10) with his children. If sold to a resident alien, to be always redeemable, at a price proportioned to the distance of the jubilee. (Leviticus 25:47-54) Foreign slaves to be held and inherited as property forever, (Leviticus 25:45,46) and fugitive slaves from foreign nations not to be given up. (23:15) (d) STRANGERS.—These seem never to have been sui juris, or able to protect themselves, and accordingly protection and kindness toward them are enjoined as a sacred duty. (Exodus 22:21; Leviticus 19:33,34) • LAW OF THINGS. (a) LAWS OF LAND (AND PROPERTY).— (1) All land to be the property of God alone, and its holders to be deemed his tenants. (Leviticus 25:23) (2) All sold land therefore to return to its original owners at the jubilee, and the price of sale to be calculated accordingly; and redemption on equitable terms to be allowed at all times. (Leviticus 25:25-27) A house sold to be redeemable within a year; and if not redeemed, to pass away altogether, ch. (Leviticus 25:29,30) But the houses of the Levites, or those in unwalled villages, to be redeemable at all times, in the same way as land; and the Levitical suburbs to be inalienable. ch. (Leviticus 25:31-34) (3) Land or houses sanctified, or tithes, or unclean firstlings, to be capable of being redeemed, at six-fifths value (calculated according to the distance from the jubilee year by the priest); if devoted by the owner and unredeemed, to be hallowed at the jubilee forever, and given to the priests; if only by a possessor, to return to the owner at the jubilee. (Leviticus 27:14-34) (4) Inheritance . (b) LAWS OF DEBT.— (1) All debts (to an Israelite) to be released at the seventh (sabbatical year; a blessing promised to obedience, and a curse on refusal to lend. (15:1-11) (2) Usury (from Israelites) not to be taken. (Exodus 22:25-27; 23:19,20) (3) Pledges not to be insolently or ruinously exacted. (24:6,10-13,17,18) (c) TAXATION.— (1) Census-money, a poll-tax (of a half shekel), to be paid for the service of the tabernacle. (Exodus 30:12-16) All spoil in war to be halved; of the combatants’ half, one five-hundreth, of the people’s, one fiftieth, to be paid for a “heave offering” to Jehovah. (2) Tithes .— (a) Tithes of all produce to be given for maintenance of the Levites. (Numbers 18:20-24) (Of this one tenth to be paid as a heave offering for maintenance of the priests. vs. (Numbers 18:24-32)) (b) Second tithe to be bestowed in religious feasting and charity, either at the holy place or (every third year) at home. (14:22-28) (c) First-fruits of corn, wine and oil (at least one sixtieth, generally one fortieth, for the priests) to be offered at Jerusalem, with a solemn declaration of dependence on God the King of Israel. (Numbers 18:12,13; 26:1-15) Firstlings of clean beasts; the redemption money (five shekels) of man and (half shekel, or one shekel) of unclean beasts to be given to the priests after sacrifice. (Numbers 18:15-18) (3) Poor laws.— (a) Gleanings (in field or vineyard) to be a legal right of the poor. (Leviticus 19:9,10; 24:19-22) (b) Slight trespass (eating on the spot) to be allowed as legal. (23:24,25) (c) Wages to be paid day by day. (24:15) (4) Maintenance of priests. (Numbers 18:8-32) (a) Tenth of Levites’ tithe . (See 2a.) (b) The heave and wave offerings (breast and right shoulder of all peace offerings). (c) The meat and sin offerings, to be eaten solemnly and only in the holy place. (c) First-fruits and redemption money. (See 2c.) (e) Price of all devoted things, unless specially given for a sacred service. A man’s service, or that of his household, to be redeemed at 50 shekels for man, 30 for woman, 20 for boy and 10 for girl. II. LAWS CRIMINAL. • OFFENCES AGAINST God(of the nature of treason.) 1St Command. Acknowledgment of false gods, (Exodus 22:20) as e.g. Molech, (Leviticus 20:1-5) and generally all idolatry . (13; 17:2-5) 2Nd Command. Witchcraft and false prophecy. (Exodus 22:18; 18:9-22; Leviticus 19:31) 3Rd Command. Blasphemy . (Leviticus 24:15,16) 4Th Command. Sabbath-breaking . (Numbers 15:32,36) Punishment in all cases, death by stoning . Idolatrous cities to be utterly destroyed. • OFFENCES AGAINST Man. 5Th Command. Disobedience to or cursing or smiting of parents, (Exodus 21:15,17; Leviticus 20:9; 21:18-21) to be punished by death by stoning, publicly adjudged and inflicted; so also of disobedience to the priests (as judges) or the Supreme Judge. Comp. (1 Kings 21:10-14) (Naboth); (2 Chronicles 24:21) (Zechariah). 6Th Command. (1) Murder to be punished by death without sanctuary or reprieve, or satisfaction. (Exodus 21:12,14; 19:11-13) Death of a slave, actually under the rod, to be punished. (Exodus 21:20,21) (2) Death by negligence to be punished by death. (Exodus 21:28-30) (3) Accidental homicide : the avenger of blood to seek safety by flight to a city of refuge, there to remain till the death of the high priest. (Numbers 35:9-28; 4:41-43; 19:4-10) (4) Uncertain murder to be expiated by formal disavowal and sacrifice by the elders of the nearest city. (21:1-9) (5) Assault to be punished by lex talionis, or damages. (Exodus 21:18,19,22-25; Leviticus 24:19,20) 7Th Command. (1) Adultery to be punished by death of both offenders; the rape of a married or betrothed woman, by death of the offender. (22:13-27) (2) Rape or seduction of an unbetrothed virgin to be compensated by marriage, with dowry (50 shekels), and without power of divorce; or, if she be refused, by payment of full dowry. (Exodus 22:16,17; 22:28,29) (3) Unlawful marriages (incestuous, etc.) to be punished, some by death, some by childlessness. (Leviticus 20:1) ... 8Th command. (1) Theft to be punished by fourfold or double restitution; or nocturnal robber might be slain as an outlaw. (Exodus 22:1-4) (2) Trespass and injury of things lent to be compensated. (Exodus 23:5-15) (3) Perversion of justice (by bribes, threats, etc.), and especially oppression of strangers, strictly forbidden. (Exodus 22:9) etc. (4) Kidnapping to be punished by death. (24:7) 9Th Command. False witness to be punished by lex talionis . (Exodus 23:1-3; 19:16-21) Slander of a wife’s chastity, by fine and loss of power of divorce. (22:18,19) A fuller consideration of the tables of the Ten Commandments is given elsewhere. [Ten Commandments COMMANDMENTS] III. LAWS JUDICIAL AND CONSTITUTIONAL. • JURISDICTION. (a) Local judges (generally Levites as more skilled in the law) appointed, for ordinary matters, probably by the people with approbation of the supreme authority (as of Moses in the wilderness), (Exodus 18:25; 1:15-18) through all the land. (16:18) (b) Appeal to the priests (at the holy place), or to the judge ; their sentence final, and to be accepted under pain of death. See (17:8-13) comp. appeal to Moses, (Exodus 18:26) (c) Two witnesses (at least) required in capital matters. (Numbers 35:30; 17:6,7) (d) Punishment, except by special command, to be personal, and not to extend to the family. (24:16) Stripes allowed and limited, (25:1-3) so as to avoid outrage on the human frame. All this would be to a great extent set aside—1st. By the summary jurisdiction of the king, see (1 Samuel 22:11-19) (Saul); (2 Samuel 12:1-5; 14:4-11; 1 Kings 3:16-28) which extended even to the deposition of the high priest. (1 Samuel 22:17,18; 1 Kings 2:26,27) The practical difficulty of its being carried out is seen in (2 Samuel 15:2-6) and would lead of course to a certain delegation of his power. 2Nd. By the appointment of the Seventy, (Numbers 11:24-30) with a solemn religious sanction. In later times there was a local sanhedrin of twenty-three in each city, and two such in Jerusalem, as well as the Great Sanhedrin, consisting of seventy members, besides the president, who was to be the high priest if duly qualified, and controlling even the king and high priest. The members were priest, scribes (Levites), and elders (of other tribes). A court of exactly this nature is noticed as appointed to supreme power by Jehoshaphat. See (2 Chronicles 19:8-11) • ROYAL POWER. The king’s power limited by the law, as written and formally accepted by the king; and directly forbidden to be despotic. (Military conquest discouraged by the prohibition of the use of horses. See (Joshua 11:6) For an example of obedience to this law see (2 Samuel 8:4) and of disobedience to it see (1 Kings 10:26-29) (17:14-20) comp. 1Sam 10:25Yet he had power of taxation (to one tenth) and of compulsory service, (1 Samuel 8:10-18) the declaration of war, (1 Samuel 11:1) ... etc. There are distinct traces of a “mutual contract,” (2 Samuel 5:3) a “league,” (2 Kings 11:17) the remonstrance with Rehoboam being clearly not extraordinary. (1 Kings 13:1-6) The princes of the congregation .—The heads of the tribes, see (Joshua 9:15) seem to have had authority under Joshua to act for the people, comp. (1 Chronicles 27:16-22) and in the later times “the princes of Judah” seem to have had power to control both the king and the priests. See (Jeremiah 26:10-24; 38:4,5) etc. • ROYAL REVENUE. (1) Tenth of produce. (2) Domain land. (1 Chronicles 27:26-29) Note confiscation of criminal’s land. (1 Kings 21:15) (3) Bond service, (1 Kings 5:17,18) chiefly on foreigners. (1 Kings 9:20-22; 2 Chronicles 2:16,17) (4) Flocks and herds. (1 Chronicles 27:29-31) (5) Tributes (gifts) from foreign kings. (6) Commerce ; especially in Solomon’s time. (1 Kings 10:22,29) etc. IV. ECCLESIASTICAL AND CEREMONIAL LAW. • LAW OF Sacrifice(considered as the sign and the appointed means of the union with God, on which the holiness of the people depended). A. ORDINARY SACRIFICES. (a) The whole burnt offering, (Leviticus 1:1) ... of the herd or the flock; to be offered continually, (Exodus 29:38-42) and the fire on the altar never to be extinguished. (Leviticus 6:8-13) (b) The meat offering, (Leviticus 2; 6:14-23) of flour, oil and frankincense, unleavened and seasoned with salt. (c) The peace offering, (Leviticus 3:1; Leviticus 7:11-21) of the herd or the flock; either a thank offering or a vow or free-will offering. (d) The sin offering or trespass offering . Le 4,5,6(A) For sins committed in ignorance. Le 4(B) For vows unwittingly made and broken, or uncleanness unwittingly contracted. Levi 5 (C) For sins wittingly committed. (Leviticus 6:1-7) b. EXTRAORDINARY SACRIFICES. (a) At the consecration of priests. Le 8,9(b) At the purification of women. Le 12(c) At the cleansing of lepers. Le 13,14(d) On the great day of atonement. Le 16(e) On the great festivals. Le 23 • LAW OF HOLINESS (arising from the union with God through sacrifice). a. HOLINESS OF PERSONS. (1) Holiness of the whole people as “children of God,” (Exodus 19:5,6; Leviticus 11-15,17,18; 14:1-21) shown in (a) The dedication of the first-born, (Exodus 13:2,12,13; 22:29,30) etc.; and the offering of all firstlings and first-fruits. Deuteronomy 26, etc. (b) Distinction of clean and unclean food. Levi 11; Deuteronomy 14. (c) Provision for purification. Levi 12,13,14,15; (23:1-4) (d) Laws against disfigurement. (Leviticus 19:27; 14:1) comp. (25:3) against excessive scourging. (e) Laws against unnatural marriages and lusts. Le 18,20(2) Holiness of the priests (and Levites) . (a) Their consecration. Le 8,9; Ex 29 (b) Their special qualifications and restrictions. (Leviticus 21:1; Leviticus 22:1-9) (c) Their rights, (18:1-6; Numbers 18:1) ... and authority. (17:8-13) b. HOLINESS OF PLACES AND THINGS. (a) The tabernacle with the ark, the vail, the altars, the laver, the priestly robes, etc. Ex 25-28,30. (b) The holy place chosen for the permanent erection of the tabernacle, (12:1; 14:22-29) where only all sacrifices were to be offered and all tithes, firstfruits, vows, etc., to be given or eaten. c. HOLINESS OF TIMES. (a) The Sabbath. (Exodus 20:9-11; 23:12) etc. (b) The sabbatical year. (Exodus 23:10,11; Leviticus 25:1-7) etc. (c) The year of jubilee. (Leviticus 25:8-16) etc. (d) The passover. (Exodus 12:3-27; Leviticus 23:4,5) (e) The feast of weeks (pentecost). (Leviticus 23:15) etc. (f) The feast of tabernacles . (Leviticus 23:33-43) (g) The feast of trumpets. (Leviticus 23:23-25) (h) The day of atonement . (Leviticus 23:26-32) etc. Such is the substance of the Mosaic law. The leading principle of the whole is its THEOCRATIC CHARACTER, its reference, that is, of all action and thoughts of men directly and immediately to the will of God. It follows from this that it is to be regarded not merely as a law, that is, a rule of conduct based on known truth and acknowledged authority, but also as a revelation of God’s nature and his dispensations. But this theocratic character of the law depends necessarily on the belief in God, as not only the creator and sustainer of the world, but as, by special covenant, the head of the Jewish nation. This immediate reference to God as their king is clearly seen as the groundwork of their whole polity. From this theocratic nature of the law follow important deductions with regard to (a) the view which it takes of political society; (b) the extent of the scope of the law; (c) the penalties by which it is enforced; and (d) the character which it seeks to impress on the people. (a) The Mosaic law seeks the basis of its polity, first, in the absolute sovereignty of God; next, in the relationship of each individual to God, and through God to his countrymen. It is clear that such a doctrine, while it contradicts none of the common theories, yet lies beneath them all. (b) The law, as proceeding directly from God and referring directly to him, is necessarily absolute in its supremacy and unlimited in its scope. It is supreme over the governors, as being only the delegates of the Lord, and therefore it is incompatible with any despotic authority in them. On the other hand, it is supreme over the governed, recognizing no inherent rights in the individual as prevailing against or limiting the law. It regulated the whole life of an Israelite. His actions were rewarded and punished with great minuteness and strictness—and that according to the standard, not of their consequences but of their intrinsic morality. (c) The penalties and rewards by which the law is enforced are such as depend on the direct theocracy. With regard to individual actions, it may be noticed that, as generally some penalties are inflicted by the subordinate and some only the supreme authority, so among the Israelites some penalties came from the hand of man, some directly from the providence of God. (d) But perhaps the most important consequence of the theocratic nature of the law was the peculiar character of goodness which it sought to impress on the people. The Mosaic law, beginning with piety as its first object, enforces most emphatically the purity essential to those who, by their union with God, have recovered the hope of intrinsic goodness, while it views righteousness and love rather as deductions from these than as independent objects. The appeal is not to any dignity of human nature, but to the obligations of communion with a holy God. The subordination, therefore, of this idea also to the religious idea is enforced; and so long as the due supremacy of the latter was preserved, all other duties would find their places in proper harmony.
